headline: High: TREK’s collaborative, browser/MCP-enabled defaults can amplify unsafe cross-agent actions; LightZero is mostly inert but offers no isolation guarantees.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: TREK uses browsers and MCP, so it can ingest external content and structured tool outputs by default; if LightZero’s outputs are copied into TREK or routed through a shared MCP/workspace, prompt injection becomes plausible. LightZero itself has no shared channel or ingestion surface documented, so the pathway is interaction-dependent and uncertain, not none.
conditions: IF TREK ingests LightZero-generated text through MCP, browser automation, or copy-paste
IF a shared workspace or message queue is introduced between the agents
mitigations: Disable MCP routes that accept untrusted text
Require manual review before TREK acts on LightZero output
Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Add provenance tags to all inter-agent messages
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at the handoff

B_data_leakage.rationale: TREK touches sensitive travel data, secrets, and files, while LightZero is documented as non-networked and non-filesystem-writing. If they share a workspace or TREK reads files produced by LightZero, leakage can occur through TREK’s uploads/logs or browser/API paths. The pair lacks a documented isolation boundary, so uncertainty pushes this above low.
conditions: IF both agents can access the same directory or uploaded artifacts
IF TREK logs or uploads content derived from LightZero outputs
mitigations: Do not place secrets in shared files
Rotate any exposed API keys or MFA secrets

C_capability_conflict.rationale: LightZero has no write, shell, subprocess, or network capabilities, so it cannot contend for mutable resources with TREK in the documented profiles. TREK does have collaborative real-time sessions and file-backed state, but without overlapping write surfaces from LightZero the conflict pathway is limited and small.
conditions: IF LightZero is extended with write or network permissions
IF both agents are later granted write access to the same files or database
mitigations: Document ownership of each writable path
requires-engineering: add locking around shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: TREK is a real-time collaborative planner with AI built in, so it may treat upstream text as actionable. LightZero can generate game-related outputs, but no verification or citation pipeline is documented between them. If LightZero output is forwarded into TREK, TREK could render or act on it without validation, creating a plausible cascade.
conditions: IF LightZero output is forwarded into TREK as planning input
IF TREK’s AI layer acts without a verification step
mitigations: Require source citations on imported text
Limit TREK actions to suggestions only
requires-engineering: add validation before downstream actions

E_compliance.rationale: TREK explicitly handles travel plans, reservations, documents, user accounts, email addresses, confirmation numbers, API keys, and MFA secrets, which creates compliance and retention obligations. LightZero is open-source game-playing software with no documented sensitive-data handling, so the compliance risk is driven by TREK alone; the pair inherits TREK’s obligations when used together.
conditions: IF TREK stores or logs travel documents, account data, or secrets
IF the deployment processes EU PII or regulated travel records
